result.topic_en: Reduction of repeated angle observations of 20 February 1807 for corrections p, a, b, c and distance, followed by the rigorous formulas for the parallaxes in longitude, latitude and distance.
result.transcription:
Noch einmal am 20 febr. 1807.
$v = 60^\circ 29' 5''$ Hieraus $p+a = 0' 45''5$ $A=120^\circ$
$h = 60.29.42$ $b = +27''$
$v' = 60.30.35$ $c = 5' 39''25$
$h' = 60.28.10$
$V = 60.41.0$ Entfernung circa 295 meter
also $p = 86''5$
$a = -41''$
$\overset{*}{B} = 60^\circ 29' 23''5$
$B = 60\ 29.22.5$ $\Big\}$ $60.29.23$

Die strengen Formeln für die Parallaxen

I. $\sin(\lambda'-\lambda) = \frac{\sin p.\cos B.\sin\lambda'}{\cos b}$

II. $\sin(b'-b) = \sin p.\left\{\frac{\cos\frac{1}{2}(\lambda'+\lambda)}{\cos\frac{1}{2}(\lambda'-\lambda)}\cos B.\sin b' - \sin B\cos b'\right\}$

III. $\Delta = 1 - \sin p.\frac{\cos\frac{1}{2}(z'+z)}{\cos\frac{1}{2}(z'-z)}$

methods.what: Reduction of observed angles to corrections p+a, b, c, then separation of p and a using a distance of about 295 m, giving two values of B and their mean
